name: Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar, Meet)
dataHosting: US default; EU on higher tiers
keyRisks: Data subject to US CLOUD Act. Extensive tracking feeds ad/AI models. Free tier eliminated for orgs. Data export possible but complex. EU hosting only on expensive plans.

name: Gmail (free/personal)
keyRisks: All email scanned for ads/AI. No data residency options. Not GDPR compliant for organisational use. Easy to leave but contacts/history lost.

name: Microsoft 365 (Outlook, OneDrive, Word, Excel, Teams, SharePoint)
keyRisks: UK hosting available but parent co. still US-jurisdicted. Deepest lock-in of any suite. Prices risen ~25% in 3 years. Copilot/AI trains on your data by default.

name: Microsoft Teams
keyRisks: Tightly bundled with M365 — near-impossible to use alternatives. Metadata extensively collected. Requires M365 licence.

name: Slack
keyRisks: Acquired by Salesforce 2021. Data in US. Free tier: 90-day history limit. Paid plans expensive for small orgs. Good data export.

name: Zoom
keyRisks: Updated ToS 2023 allowing AI training on calls. Data routed through US. Low lock-in. Prices increased.

name: WhatsApp (organisational use)
keyRisks: Metadata harvested even with E2E encryption. Owned by Meta. Not suitable for sensitive organisational comms. No group data export.

name: Dropbox
keyRisks: Data in US. Moderate tracking. Reasonable export. Easy to switch. Prices have increased.

name: Salesforce
keyRisks: Extremely deep lock-in. Proprietary data model. Very expensive. Migration is a major project. EU hosting available.

name: HubSpot
keyRisks: Data in US. Freemium hooks you in, prices escalate. Proprietary data model. Tracks website visitors extensively.

name: Canva
keyRisks: Data on US infrastructure. Teams prices increased 300% in 2024. AI features train on content. Templates/brand kits create dependency.

name: Mailchimp
keyRisks: Acquired by Intuit. Free tier severely cut. Data shared across Intuit products. Significant price increases since acquisition.

name: Trello
keyRisks: Owned by Atlassian. Data in US. Free tier limited. Low lock-in — easy to export and switch.

name: Monday.com
keyRisks: Data in US. Expensive per-seat pricing. Moderate lock-in through workflows. Tracks usage for AI.

name: Asana
keyRisks: Data in US. Per-seat pricing. Moderate lock-in. AI features in development. Good data export. Increasingly expensive.

name: WordPress.com (hosted)
keyRisks: Hosted version is US-based. Self-hosted WordPress.org is open source and excellent. Lock-in through proprietary themes/plugins.

name: Squarespace
keyRisks: Data in US. Proprietary — cannot take your site elsewhere. Poor data export. Annual pricing creates lock-in.

name: Wix
keyRisks: Data in US. Highest lock-in of any CMS — virtually impossible to migrate. Aggressive upselling.

name: SurveyMonkey
keyRisks: Data in US. Expensive. Low lock-in (data exportable). Tracks respondent behaviour. Significant price increases.

name: Typeform
keyRisks: Spanish company but US cloud. GDPR compliant. Low lock-in. Expensive per-response pricing.

name: Google Forms
keyRisks: All responses feed Google's data ecosystem. Free but data is harvested. Tied to Google Sheets.

name: Meta (Facebook / Instagram)
keyRisks: Maximum surveillance. Data harvested for ads. Algorithmic control over reach. Community locked in platform.

name: X / Twitter
keyRisks: Under Musk: unpredictable policy changes, API restricted, staff gutted. High continuity risk. Maximum surveillance.

name: LinkedIn
keyRisks: Microsoft-owned. Extensive professional data harvesting. AI training on posts/messages. Network lock-in.

name: Calendly
keyRisks: Data in US. Calendar access is sensitive. Low lock-in. Easy to replace.

name: Eventbrite
keyRisks: Data in US. Attendee data harvested. Transaction fees. Moderate lock-in through event history.

name: Amazon Web Services
keyRisks: UK hosting available but Amazon is US-jurisdicted. Deep lock-in through proprietary services. CLOUD Act applies.

name: LibreOffice
keyRisks: Open source, self-hosted office suite. Full data sovereignty. No cloud dependency. Free to use. Wide format compatibility.

name: OnlyOffice
keyRisks: EU-based company. Self-hosted or cloud options. Compatible with MS Office formats throughout. Low lock-in.

name: Zoho Workplace
keyRisks: India-based company with EU data centre options. GDPR-compliant. Lower surveillance risk than US equivalents. No advertising model.

name: Google Meet
keyRisks: Part of Google Workspace. Data in US. Extensive surveillance across calls. Tied to Google Calendar. No standalone product — requires Google account.

name: Jitsi Meet
keyRisks: Open source video conferencing. Self-hosted for full data control. 8x8's hosted meet.jit.si runs on US servers. High flexibility, no lock-in.

name: Element (Matrix)
keyRisks: Open, decentralised protocol. Self-hosted or join any Matrix server. Full data portability. End-to-end encryption by default. No vendor lock-in.

name: Discord
keyRisks: Data in US. Terms permit broad data use including AI training. Community and message history locked in platform. Limited data export.

name: Whereby
keyRisks: Norwegian company, EU data infrastructure. GDPR-compliant. No downloads required for participants. Straightforward pricing.

name: BigBlueButton
keyRisks: Open source video conferencing designed for education. Self-hosted. No vendor lock-in. Requires technical capacity to run.

name: Donorfy
keyRisks: UK-based CRM for charities. Data hosted in UK. Good data export. Designed for UK charity sector. Some lock-in through custom reporting.

name: Beacon
keyRisks: UK-based CRM for non-profits. Data in UK. Purpose-built for the sector. Transparent pricing. Reasonable data export.

name: CiviCRM
keyRisks: Open source CRM designed for civil society organisations. Self-hosted. Full data sovereignty. No per-seat pricing. Requires technical support to maintain.

name: Lamplight
keyRisks: UK-based database for social care and community organisations. Data in UK. Purpose-built for frontline services. No external data sharing.

name: Microsoft Dynamics 365
keyRisks: Deepest lock-in in the CRM market alongside Salesforce. Tightly integrated with M365 ecosystem. Very expensive. Migration requires specialist consultants. Data under US jurisdiction.

name: SugarCRM
keyRisks: US-based CRM with EU deployment options. Moderate surveillance risk. Pricing can escalate with add-ons. Complex migrations.

name: Odoo
keyRisks: Belgian company, EU-based infrastructure. Open source core with paid hosting options. Self-hosted is genuinely viable. Standard data formats throughout.

name: Xero
keyRisks: New Zealand company with UK data hosting. GDPR-compliant for UK/EU customers. Popular in UK market. Low lock-in via standard CSV/PDF export. Prices have increased.

name: QuickBooks
keyRisks: Intuit (US) product, data in US. Prices have risen significantly post-free-tier. Moderate lock-in through historical data. Some UK-specific features but fundamentally US infrastructure.

name: Sage
keyRisks: UK-based company with UK/EU data hosting. Long-established in UK market. Moderate lock-in through proprietary file formats. Prices have increased.

name: FreeAgent
keyRisks: UK-based, owned by NatWest Group. Data in UK. Popular with UK freelancers and small businesses. Clean data export. Low lock-in.

name: Wave
keyRisks: Canadian fintech now owned by H&R Block (US). Free accounting but data in US. Limited GDPR compliance. Some features discontinued in recent years.

name: Coconut
keyRisks: UK-based fintech for freelancers and sole traders. Data in UK. Young company — some continuity risk. Transparent pricing.

name: Sage Intacct
keyRisks: Enterprise accounting platform, US-based. High lock-in through complex implementation. Very expensive. Primarily aimed at larger organisations.

name: Brevo (Sendinblue)
keyRisks: French company, EU-based data infrastructure. GDPR-compliant. Good alternative to US email marketing platforms. Transparent pricing.

name: ConvertKit (Kit)
keyRisks: US-based, data in US. Popular with creators and non-profits. Some subscriber tracking. Moderate lock-in through subscriber list formats.

name: Campaign Monitor
keyRisks: Australian company acquired by Marigold (US). Data partly in US. Standard email marketing risks. Reasonable data export. Transparent pricing.

name: Listmonk
keyRisks: Open source self-hosted email marketing. Full data sovereignty. No vendor lock-in. Requires technical capacity to set up and maintain.

name: Luma
keyRisks: US startup, data in US. Growing in events space. Relatively new — some continuity risk. Collects attendee data. Low lock-in.

name: Tito
keyRisks: Irish company, EU-based. Privacy-focused event ticketing. Good data export. Transparent pricing. No attendee data harvesting.

name: Pretix
keyRisks: German company, EU-based. Open source ticketing with hosted options. GDPR-compliant. No attendee data harvesting. Self-hosted option available.

name: Figma
keyRisks: Acquired by Adobe (US). Browser-based design tool with US data infrastructure. Proprietary .fig format creates lock-in. Prices increased post-Adobe acquisition.

name: Penpot
keyRisks: Open source design tool by Kaleidos (Spain). EU-based. Self-hosted option. Standard SVG format — no proprietary lock-in.

name: Adobe Creative Cloud
keyRisks: Deep lock-in through proprietary file formats (PSD, AI, INDD). Very expensive subscription. Aggressive pricing tiers. Data in US. Creative files non-portable without Adobe software.

name: WordPress (self-hosted)
keyRisks: Open source CMS. Self-hosted. Full data sovereignty. The most widely used CMS globally. Vast ecosystem of themes and plugins. Some plugin lock-in possible.

name: Webflow
keyRisks: US-based visual web builder. Proprietary platform — cannot export a functioning site to another host. Data in US. Prices have increased.

name: Netlify
keyRisks: US-based JAMstack hosting. Data in US. Low lock-in for static sites — can move elsewhere easily. Developer-focused. Free tier is generous.

name: Vercel
keyRisks: US-based hosting for front-end frameworks. Data in US. Growing lock-in through proprietary edge features. Free tier includes generous limits.

name: Cloudflare
keyRisks: US-based CDN and DDoS protection. Very widely used. Low lock-in for basic CDN. Increasing lock-in if using Workers/Pages/R2. Data potentially subject to US surveillance.

name: Microsoft Azure
keyRisks: Microsoft's cloud platform. Same US jurisdiction issues as M365. Deep lock-in through proprietary services. Very expensive at scale. EU hosting available but US-jurisdicted.

name: OneDrive
keyRisks: Microsoft cloud storage, deeply integrated with M365. Data in US/EU depending on plan. Difficult to leave if using M365 collaboration features.

name: Google Drive
keyRisks: Extensive data collection. Data feeds Google's AI and ad systems. Data in US. Difficult to leave if using Google Workspace. Free tier uses your data.

name: Nextcloud
keyRisks: Open source cloud storage. Self-hosted. Full data sovereignty. EU-based company for hosted options. Strong encryption. No vendor lock-in.

name: Box
keyRisks: US-based enterprise cloud storage. GDPR-compliant options. Moderate surveillance risk. Enterprise pricing. Reasonable data portability.

name: Tresorit
keyRisks: Swiss/EU company with end-to-end encryption. Zero-knowledge architecture. GDPR-compliant. Focused on security-first organisations. Relatively expensive.

name: Airtable
keyRisks: US-based, data in US. Significant lock-in through proprietary base format. Expensive per-seat pricing. AI features expanding. Popular with non-profits but costs escalate.

name: ClickUp
keyRisks: US-based all-in-one project management. Data in US. Aggressive AI feature rollout. Complex pricing. Moderate lock-in through automations.

name: Basecamp
keyRisks: US-based by 37signals. Flat-fee pricing (no per-seat). Data in US. Relatively low lock-in. Good data export. Principled stance on product bloat.

name: Taiga
keyRisks: Open source project management by Kaleidos (Spain). EU-based. Self-hosted option. No vendor lock-in. Standard data formats.

name: OpenProject
keyRisks: German open source project management. EU-based. Self-hosted option. GDPR-compliant. Used by public sector organisations.

name: Todoist
keyRisks: Estonian-run company (Doist). Privacy-focused approach. Data in EU/US. Low lock-in. Transparent pricing.

name: Facebook / Meta
keyRisks: Highest surveillance in the social media landscape. Data used for advertising targeting. Community locked on platform. Algorithmic control over reach. US jurisdiction.

name: Instagram
keyRisks: Owned by Meta. Visual-first platform with extensive data harvesting. Creator and community lock-in. Algorithmic control over reach. US jurisdiction.

name: Mastodon
keyRisks: Open source, decentralised social network. Self-hosted or join any instance. Full data portability. No advertising. EU-based core development.

name: Bluesky
keyRisks: US-based decentralised social network. AT Protocol allows data portability. Low lock-in by design. US company with evolving governance model.

name: TikTok
keyRisks: Chinese-owned (ByteDance). Highest-risk social platform. Extensive behavioural data collection. Geopolitical risk and potential bans. Algorithmic reach control.

name: YouTube
keyRisks: Google-owned. Extensive surveillance and data collection. Creator lock-in through subscriber base. US jurisdiction. Free but data-intensive.

name: Buffer
keyRisks: US-based social media scheduling. Data in US. Moderate data collection. Reasonable data export. Low lock-in compared to direct platform use.

name: Hootsuite
keyRisks: Canadian company. Social media management platform. Data primarily in US/Canada. Reasonable data portability. Moderate surveillance risk.

name: Signal
keyRisks: Non-profit foundation (US). End-to-end encrypted messaging. Minimal metadata collection. Open source protocol. Some continuity risk as donation-dependent.

name: Telegram
keyRisks: UAE-based company. Encrypted only for secret chats — group messages not encrypted by default. Opaque ownership and governance. Some risk for sensitive organisational use.

name: Proton Mail
keyRisks: Swiss company, EU-based. End-to-end encrypted email. Zero-access architecture. GDPR-compliant. Strong privacy track record. Reasonable pricing.

name: Gmail / Google Email
keyRisks: Business Gmail via Google Workspace. Data in US by default. Extensive surveillance for AI and ad systems. US CLOUD Act applies. EU hosting available on higher tiers only.

name: Outlook / Exchange
keyRisks: Microsoft email product, deeply integrated with M365. Data in US/EU. High lock-in if using calendar and contacts sync. AI features (Copilot) train on email content.

name: Tuta (Tutanota)
keyRisks: German company, EU-based. End-to-end encryption throughout. Open source client. Strong privacy. Affordable pricing for small organisations.

name: Fastmail
keyRisks: Australian company, US data centres. Not end-to-end encrypted by default. Good privacy policy. GDPR-compliant. Reasonable pricing.

name: Zoho Mail
keyRisks: India-based (Zoho). GDPR-compliant EU data centre option. Ad-free. No data harvesting for advertising. Good value.

name: ChatGPT
keyRisks: OpenAI (US). Extensive data collection. Conversations used for model training unless opted out. Maximum surveillance risk. Expensive API. Subject to US CLOUD Act.

name: Claude
keyRisks: Anthropic (US). Lower surveillance risk than OpenAI equivalents. Privacy-conscious approach. Still US-based and subject to CLOUD Act. API pricing can escalate.

name: Microsoft Copilot
keyRisks: Deepest lock-in of any AI tool — embedded throughout M365. Trains on your organisational data. Very expensive. Cannot use without M365. US jurisdiction.

name: Google Gemini
keyRisks: Google's AI suite. Highest surveillance risk — data feeds into Google's ad and AI ecosystem. Deeply integrated with Google Workspace. US jurisdiction.

name: Notion AI
keyRisks: AI features within Notion. US-based. AI trains on workspace content. Deep lock-in through Notion's proprietary data structure. Expensive for large teams.

name: Grammarly
keyRisks: US-based. AI writing assistant that reads all text you write. Some data used for product improvement. Relatively low lock-in — easy to stop using.

name: Midjourney
keyRisks: US-based AI image generation. Discord-based (US infrastructure). Images and prompts used for model training. Limited data portability.

name: DALL-E
keyRisks: OpenAI (US). Image generation tied to OpenAI ecosystem. Same privacy concerns as ChatGPT. Images and prompts may be used for training.

name: Zapier
keyRisks: US-based automation tool. All data flows through Zapier's US servers. High lock-in through complex automation workflows. Expensive per-task pricing. AI features expanding.

name: Make (Integromat)
keyRisks: Czech Republic (EU) company. Lower risk than US alternatives. Data processing in EU. Reasonable pricing. Moderate lock-in through complex scenarios.

name: Otter.ai
keyRisks: US-based meeting transcription. Extensive audio data collection. Transcripts and audio stored in US. AI features train on meeting content.

name: Fireflies.ai
keyRisks: US-based meeting transcription. Meeting recordings stored in US. AI trains on your meeting content. Participant consent questions for all-hands recordings.

name: Perplexity
keyRisks: US-based AI search engine. Data in US. Search queries and results retained. Lower lock-in than productivity AI tools. Evolving privacy policy.

name: Canva Magic Studio
keyRisks: AI features within Canva. Australian company with US infrastructure. AI trains on content you create. Increasingly integrated with core Canva workflow.

name: Power Automate
keyRisks: Microsoft automation platform. Deep integration with M365 — difficult to use independently. Very high lock-in. Data in US/EU. Replaces standalone automation tools.

name: Mistral AI
keyRisks: French company (EU). Open weight models. EU data infrastructure. Lower surveillance risk. Evolving pricing. Smaller ecosystem than US competitors.

name: Ollama
keyRisks: Open source tool for running LLMs locally. Complete data sovereignty — no data leaves your machine. Free. Requires technical capacity and adequate hardware.

name: LM Studio
keyRisks: Open source local LLM runner. Complete data sovereignty. No cloud dependency. Free. Requires modern hardware.

name: Jan
keyRisks: Open source local AI interface. Self-hosted. No data collection. Free. Technical setup required.

name: GreenPT
keyRisks: EU-based AI service focused on sustainability. Lower risk than US alternatives. EU data infrastructure. Smaller ecosystem — some continuity risk.

name: Hugging Face
keyRisks: US-based AI model hub. Models self-hosted = low risk. Using API = US data. Large open source community. Models available for local deployment.

name: Open WebUI
keyRisks: Open source local AI interface. Self-hosted. No data collection. Free. Works with Ollama and other local models.

name: Meta Llama
keyRisks: Open weight model from Meta. Can be run locally with full data sovereignty. Meta brand carries governance concerns but local deployment is genuinely private.

name: Private AI
keyRisks: Canadian company focused on privacy-preserving AI. EU and Canadian data processing. Purpose-built for organisations with sensitive data requirements.

name: Stripe
keyRisks: Irish headquarters but US-based in practice. Very widely used payments processor. Moderate lock-in through payment history. EU operations well-established.

name: GoCardless
keyRisks: UK-based direct debit payments. Data in UK/EU. Purpose-built for recurring payments. Low lock-in. GDPR-compliant.

name: PayPal
keyRisks: US-based. Extensive data collection. Transaction history lock-in. Expensive fees. Widely recognised by donors and customers.

name: JustGiving
keyRisks: Owned by Blackbaud (US). Popular fundraising platform for UK charities. Donor data held by JustGiving. Transaction fees. Moderate lock-in through fundraising history.

name: GiveWP
keyRisks: US-based donation plugin for WordPress. Data in self-hosted WordPress by default. Plugin lock-in within WordPress ecosystem. Relatively low overall risk.

name: Google Sheets
keyRisks: Google's cloud spreadsheet. Extensive data collection. Data feeds Google's ecosystem. Free but data-intensive for sensitive information. Tied to Google Drive.

name: Microsoft Excel
keyRisks: Microsoft's spreadsheet. Desktop version has low risk. Cloud (365) version has higher surveillance risk. Widely used — high switching costs for complex workbooks.

name: Microsoft Access
keyRisks: Legacy Microsoft database. Desktop only — low cloud risk. Very high lock-in through proprietary MDB format. Requires Windows. Officially supported but increasingly deprecated.

name: Notion
keyRisks: US-based all-in-one workspace. Data in US. AI features train on content. High lock-in through proprietary block-based data model. Difficult to fully export structured data.

name: Baserow
keyRisks: Dutch open source database. EU-based. Self-hosted option. API-first design. Clean data export. No vendor lock-in.

name: NocoDB
keyRisks: Open source Airtable alternative. Self-hosted. Full data sovereignty. Connects to existing databases. No vendor lock-in.

name: Supabase
keyRisks: US-based open source database platform. Open source core. Self-hosted option available. Low lock-in due to standard PostgreSQL underneath.

name: Power BI
keyRisks: Microsoft's business intelligence platform. Deep integration with M365. High lock-in through proprietary .pbix format. Data in US/EU. Expensive at enterprise scale.

name: Tableau
keyRisks: Salesforce-owned data visualisation. Very expensive licensing. High lock-in through proprietary workbook format. US jurisdiction. Enterprise-focused.

name: Looker Studio
keyRisks: Google's free data visualisation tool. Data in US. Extensive integration with Google ecosystem. Free but surveillance trade-off. Moderate lock-in through connector configuration.

name: Metabase
keyRisks: Open source business intelligence. Self-hosted option available. Low lock-in. Free for basic use. EU-friendly when self-hosted.

name: Evidence
keyRisks: Open source, code-based data visualisation. Self-hosted. Full data sovereignty. Requires development skills.

name: Impact Reporting Spreadsheet
keyRisks: Internal tool — full data sovereignty. No external risk. Only continuity risk is if the person who built it leaves or changes role.

name: QGIS
keyRisks: Open source GIS software. Self-hosted. Full data sovereignty. Industry standard for open source geospatial work. Large community.

name: ArcGIS Online
keyRisks: Esri's cloud GIS platform (US). Very high lock-in through proprietary shapefile ecosystem. Expensive licensing. Widely used in public sector but difficult to migrate away from.

name: Google Maps Platform
keyRisks: Google's mapping API. US jurisdiction. Extensive usage tracking. High lock-in if building mapping features around it. Pricing increased significantly in 2018.

name: Mapbox
keyRisks: US-based mapping platform. Data in US. Popular with developers. Reasonable data portability. Some lock-in through SDK usage.

name: Felt
keyRisks: US-based collaborative map-making tool. Data in US. Modern, easy to use. Low lock-in for simple maps.

name: CARTO
keyRisks: Spanish-US company. Specialised geospatial analytics. Some EU data options. Moderate pricing. Lock-in through proprietary analysis platform.
